attributes.residual: TWO MECHANISMS THAT NO SINGLE SOURCE FORM SUPPLIED TOGETHER -- this is the resolution stamp. (A) The target saves r31 in the prologue proper (`stw r31,20(r1)` at +0x14, immediately after the stwu); the free-function form sinks it to +0x20 because r31's first definition is late. (B) The target homes `this` in its parameter save slot and reloads it (`stw r3,8(r1)` at +0x18, `lwz r31,8(r1)` at +0x24), reusing r3 as scratch for the second vtable address. MEASURED: writing the function as a real `MoviePlayer::MoviePlayer()` member FIXES (A) exactly -- the save lands at +0x14 -- but then never produces (B), capping at 24 instructions against the target's 25. The retained free-function form gets (B) free from its `volatile` parameter and misses (A), scoring real 2 at 25/25. Four constructor forms were measured and none recovered (B): plain `self = (u32*)this` (real 7), member-array `words[]` access (real 7, NEUTRAL - two identical results kill the natural-access axis), a `volatile` home local (real 11, adds a store and forces stmw), and hoisting both vtable addresses into temps so both are simultaneously live as in the target (real 17, multiset back to 3t, still 24 insns). The likely honest resolution, NOT attempted because it would disturb an exact sibling: real member sub-objects at +32 and +336 constructed through a member-init list, whose -Cpp_exceptions cleanup is what would home `this`. That is a whole-class restructure and the class map records why MoviePlayer is deliberately spelled without its base.
